0849| def _recording_login_shell(directory: Path, probe: Path, real_shell: str) -> Path:

0619| # Run a command under a hard time bound. ``timeout`` from GNU coreutils is not
0620| # required and is not used: the command runs in the background, a watchdog
0621| # sends a graceful stop when the bound elapses and forcefully stops whatever
0622| # remains of the process tree after the grace period, and the caller returns
0623| # as soon as the command itself is done. Nothing the function starts survives
0624| # it. CHECK_STATUS is 124 when the bound elapsed.
0625| #
0626| # The checked command is deliberately *not* given its own process group here.
0627| # ``set -m`` makes the shell put the background job in a background process
0628| # group, and an interactive login shell in that position stops on its first
0629| # terminal access instead of answering, which is exactly the hang this check
0630| # must not have. The process tree walk in ``signal_run`` reaches everything the
0631| # shell forked without it.
0632| bounded_run() {
0633|     limit=$1
0634|     shift
0635|     grace=$(verify_grace)
0636|     poll=$(verify_poll)

0638|     CHECK_OUTPUT=
0639|     if ! create_check_dir; then
0640|         return 1
0641|     fi
0642|     out=$CHECK_DIR/output
0643|     timed_out=$CHECK_DIR/timed-out
0644|     saved_umask=$(umask)
0645|     umask 077
0646|     if ! : > "$out"; then
0647|         umask "$saved_umask"
0648|         cleanup_check
0649|         return 1
0650|     fi
0651|     "$@" > "$out" 2>/dev/null < /dev/null &
0652|     CHECK_CHILD=$!
0653|     umask "$saved_umask"
0654|     child=$CHECK_CHILD
0655|     (
0656|         exec > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null
0657|         sleeper=
0658|         trap 'kill "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 0' TERM
0659|         # A partial second poll only works where ``sleep`` understands one; fall
0660|         # back to whole seconds so the bound never elapses early.
0661|         if [ $((poll % 1000)) -ne 0 ] && ! sleep 0.001 2>/dev/null; then
0662|             poll=1000
0663|         fi
0664|         limit_ms=$((limit * 1000))
0665|         elapsed_ms=0
0666|         while [ "$elapsed_ms" -lt "$limit_ms" ]; do
0667|             pause=$poll
0668|             remaining=$((limit_ms - elapsed_ms))
0669|             if [ "$pause" -gt "$remaining" ]; then
0670|                 pause=$remaining
0671|             fi
0672|             delay=$((pause / 1000))
0673|             if [ $((pause % 1000)) -ne 0 ]; then
0674|                 delay=$(printf '%d.%03d' "$delay" $((pause % 1000)))
0675|             fi
0676|             sleep "$delay" &
0677|             sleeper=$!
0678|             wait "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true
0679|             sleeper=
0680|             elapsed_ms=$((elapsed_ms + pause))
0681|             if ! kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; then
0682|                 exit 0
0683|             fi
0684|         done
0685|         : > "$timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
0686|         signal_run TERM "$child"
0687|         sleep "$grace" 2>/dev/null || true
0688|         signal_run KILL "$child"
0689|     ) &
0690|     CHECK_WATCHER=$!
0691|     wait "$child" || CHECK_STATUS=$?
0692|     CHECK_CHILD=
0693|     if [ -e "$timed_out" ]; then
0694|         # The watchdog still owns the graceful then the forceful stop; let it
0695|         # finish so nothing outlives the check.
0696|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0697|         CHECK_STATUS=124

0699|         kill -TERM "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0700|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0701|     fi
0702|     CHECK_WATCHER=
0703|     CHECK_OUTPUT=$(cat "$out") || CHECK_OUTPUT=
0704|     cleanup_check
0705|     return 0
0706| }

0907| def _recording_login_shell(directory: Path, probe: Path, real_shell: str) -> Path:
0908|     """A handled shell name that records the check's directory, then runs ``real_shell``.
0909| 
0910|     ``ls -ld`` output of every ``forgel-code-check.*`` entry goes into ``probe``,
0911|     so the test can inspect the permissions of a directory that no longer exists
0912|     by the time the installer returns. The entries sit in the temporary tree of
0913|     the test, next to the checked shell's own ``$HOME``.

0916|     stub = directory / "bash"

0918|         "#!/bin/sh\nprobe=%s\n" % _shell_quote(probe)
0919|         + 'ls -ld "$(dirname "$HOME")/tmp"/%s.* > "$probe/entries" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
0920|         % CHECK_PREFIX
0921|         + 'exec %s "$@"\n' % _shell_quote(real_shell),
0922|         encoding="utf-8",
0923|     )
0924|     stub.chmod(0o755)

0302| # directory is prepended only when it is not already in PATH, so sourcing the
0303| # block twice, or from several profiles, leaves one entry in PATH.
0304| print_block() {
0305|     printf '%s\n' "$MARKER_START"
0306|     printf 'case ":$PATH:" in\n'
0307|     printf '    *":%s:"*) ;;\n' "$BIN_DIR"
0308|     printf '    *) PATH="%s:$PATH" ;;\n' "$BIN_DIR"
0309|     printf 'esac\n'
0310|     printf 'export PATH\n'
0311|     printf '%s\n' "$MARKER_END"

0314| # Whether the last byte of the file is a newline.
0315| ends_with_newline() {

0317|     [ "$(tail -c 1 "$1" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = "1" ]

0320| # Whether a start marker is left open, without an end marker after it. Such a
0321| # block is not a block: where it ends is unknown, so it is never removed and the
0322| # file is left exactly as it is. Status 0 means an open marker was found, 1 a
0323| # well-formed or marker-free file, anything else that the file is unreadable.
0324| has_unclosed_block() {
0325|     awk -v start="$MARKER_START" -v end="$MARKER_END" '
0326|         $0 == start { inside = 1; next }
0327|         $0 == end { inside = 0 }
0328|         END { exit (inside ? 0 : 1) }
0329|     ' "$1"
0330| }

0332| # Drop the marked block, if there is one. Every other line is kept byte for
0333| # byte, including whether the file ended with a newline: the rewrite carries
0334| # the last line without a terminator when the input had none. A block this
0335| # installer appended after a last line that had no final newline carries the
0336| # separator comment, and both go away, so uninstall restores the original. An
0337| # unterminated start marker is reported and the file is left untouched, because
0338| # removing everything from that marker on would delete unrelated content.
0339| remove_profile_block() {
0340|     profile=$1
0341|     if [ ! -f "$profile" ]; then
0342|         return 0
0343|     fi
0344|     if ! grep -Fq "$MARKER_START" "$profile"; then
0345|         return 0
0346|     fi
0347|     scan=0
0348|     has_unclosed_block "$profile" || scan=$?
0349|     case $scan in
0350|         0)
0351|             echo "install.sh: $profile has a '$MARKER_START' line with no matching '$MARKER_END' line; leaving the file unchanged. Repair that block and run install.sh again." >&2
0352|             return 1
0353|             ;;
0354|         1) ;;
0355|         *)
0356|             echo "install.sh: cannot read $profile" >&2
0357|             return 1
0358|             ;;
0359|     esac
0360|     tmp=$profile.forgel-code.$$
0361|     if ! cp -p "$profile" "$tmp"; then
0362|         echo "install.sh: cannot write next to $profile" >&2
0363|         return 1
0364|     fi
0365|     final_newline=0
0366|     if ends_with_newline "$profile"; then
0367|         final_newline=1
0368|     fi
0369|     if ! awk -v start="$MARKER_START" -v end="$MARKER_END" \
0370|             -v separator="$MARKER_SEPARATOR" -v final_newline="$final_newline" '
0371|             { text[NR] = $0 }
0372|             END {
0373|                 total = NR
0374|                 kept = 0
0375|                 inside = 0
0376|                 block_end = 0
0377|                 for (i = 1; i <= total; i++) {
0378|                     if (inside == 0 && text[i] == start) {
0379|                         inside = 1
0380|                         block_end = 0
0381|                         continue
0382|                     }
0383|                     if (inside == 1) {
0384|                         if (text[i] == end) {
0385|                             inside = 0
0386|                             block_end = i
0387|                         }
0388|                         continue
0389|                     }
0390|                     kept++
0391|                     kept_text[kept] = text[i]
0392|                     kept_index[kept] = i
0393|                 }

0395|                 if (block_end == total && kept > 0 && kept_text[kept] == separator) {
0396|                     kept--
0397|                     restore_missing_newline = 1
0398|                 }
0399|                 for (i = 1; i <= kept; i++) {
0400|                     terminate = 1
0401|                     if (i == kept && restore_missing_newline == 1) {
0402|                         terminate = 0
0403|                     } else if (i == kept && kept_index[i] == total && final_newline == 0) {
0404|                         terminate = 0
0405|                     }
0406|                     if (terminate) {
0407|                         printf "%s\n", kept_text[i]
0408|                     } else {
0409|                         printf "%s", kept_text[i]
0410|                     }
0411|                 }
0412|             }
0413|         ' "$profile" > "$tmp"; then
0414|         rm -f "$tmp"
0415|         echo "install.sh: cannot rewrite $profile" >&2
0416|         return 1

0421|         return 1
0422|     fi

0426| # Exactly one block, whatever the profile already held. The previous block is
0427| # removed first and only then is the new one appended, so an interrupted run
0428| # leaves one block at most. The append is byte-stable: a second run over the
0429| # same profile rewrites it to the same bytes, and a last line without a final
0430| # newline is recorded so the block can be dropped without leaving a newline

0442|             printf '\n'
0443|             printf '%s\n' "$MARKER_SEPARATOR"
0444|         fi
0445|         print_block

0499| # An unpredictable name component, so the check directory cannot be guessed

0507|         ''|*[!0-9a-f]*) token= ;;

0535| # The members of a process group, one pid per line.
0536| process_group() {

0540| # Every descendant of a process, one pid per line.
0541| process_tree() {
0542|     ps -A -o pid= -o ppid= 2>/dev/null | awk -v root="$1" '
0543|         { parent[$1] = $2; ids[NR] = $1 }
0544|         END {
0545|             frontier[0] = root
0546|             count = 1
0547|             for (i = 0; i < count; i++) {
0548|                 for (j = 1; j <= NR; j++) {
0549|                     pid = ids[j]
0550|                     if (parent[pid] == frontier[i] && !(pid in seen)) {
0551|                         seen[pid] = 1
0552|                         frontier[count] = pid
0553|                         count++
0554|                     }
0555|                 }
0556|             }
0557|             for (i = 1; i < count; i++) print frontier[i]

0561| # Signal a process and every process it started. When the process leads its own
0562| # process group the whole group is signalled, so a shell that forked cannot
0563| # leave anything behind; otherwise the process tree is walked. The checked
0564| # command is started in the installer's own process group on purpose, so this
0565| # never signals the installer itself.
0566| signal_run() {
0567|     signal=$1
0568|     root=$2
0569|     if [ -z "$root" ]; then
0570|         return 0
0571|     fi
0572|     targets=
0573|     if command -v ps >/dev/null 2>&1; then
0574|         group=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$root" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ') || group=
0575|         own=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ') || own=
0576|         case $group in
0577|             ''|*[!0-9]*) group= ;;
0578|         esac
0579|         if [ -n "$group" ] && [ "$group" != "$own" ]; then
0580|             targets=$(process_group "$group")
0581|         fi
0582|     fi
0583|     if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
0584|         targets=$(process_tree "$root")
0585|     fi
0586|     for pid in $targets; do
0587|         kill -"$signal" "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
0588|     done
0589|     kill -"$signal" "$root" 2>/dev/null || true
0590|     return 0

0599|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true

0619| # Run a command under a hard time bound. ``timeout`` from GNU coreutils is not
0620| # required and is not used: the command runs in the background, a watchdog
0621| # sends a graceful stop when the bound elapses and forcefully stops whatever
0622| # remains of the process tree after the grace period, and the caller returns
0623| # as soon as the command itself is done. Nothing the function starts survives
0624| # it. CHECK_STATUS is 124 when the bound elapsed.
0625| #
0626| # The checked command is deliberately *not* given its own process group here.
0627| # ``set -m`` makes the shell put the background job in a background process
0628| # group, and an interactive login shell in that position stops on its first
0629| # terminal access instead of answering, which is exactly the hang this check
0630| # must not have. The process tree walk in ``signal_run`` reaches everything the
0631| # shell forked without it.
0632| bounded_run() {
0633|     limit=$1
0634|     shift
0635|     grace=$(verify_grace)
0636|     poll=$(verify_poll)
0637|     CHECK_STATUS=0
0638|     CHECK_OUTPUT=
0639|     if ! create_check_dir; then
0640|         return 1
0641|     fi
0642|     out=$CHECK_DIR/output
0643|     timed_out=$CHECK_DIR/timed-out
0644|     saved_umask=$(umask)
0645|     umask 077
0646|     if ! : > "$out"; then
0647|         umask "$saved_umask"
0648|         cleanup_check
0649|         return 1
0650|     fi
0651|     "$@" > "$out" 2>/dev/null < /dev/null &
0652|     CHECK_CHILD=$!
0653|     umask "$saved_umask"
0654|     child=$CHECK_CHILD
0655|     (
0656|         exec > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null
0657|         sleeper=
0658|         trap 'kill "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 0' TERM
0659|         # A partial second poll only works where ``sleep`` understands one; fall
0660|         # back to whole seconds so the bound never elapses early.
0661|         if [ $((poll % 1000)) -ne 0 ] && ! sleep 0.001 2>/dev/null; then
0662|             poll=1000
0663|         fi
0664|         limit_ms=$((limit * 1000))
0665|         elapsed_ms=0
0666|         while [ "$elapsed_ms" -lt "$limit_ms" ]; do
0667|             pause=$poll
0668|             remaining=$((limit_ms - elapsed_ms))
0669|             if [ "$pause" -gt "$remaining" ]; then
0670|                 pause=$remaining
0671|             fi
0672|             delay=$((pause / 1000))
0673|             if [ $((pause % 1000)) -ne 0 ]; then
0674|                 delay=$(printf '%d.%03d' "$delay" $((pause % 1000)))
0675|             fi
0676|             sleep "$delay" &
0677|             sleeper=$!
0678|             wait "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true
0679|             sleeper=
0680|             elapsed_ms=$((elapsed_ms + pause))
0681|             if ! kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; then
0682|                 exit 0
0683|             fi
0684|         done
0685|         : > "$timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
0686|         signal_run TERM "$child"
0687|         sleep "$grace" 2>/dev/null || true
0688|         signal_run KILL "$child"
0689|     ) &
0690|     CHECK_WATCHER=$!
0691|     wait "$child" || CHECK_STATUS=$?
0692|     CHECK_CHILD=
0693|     if [ -e "$timed_out" ]; then
0694|         # The watchdog still owns the graceful then the forceful stop; let it
0695|         # finish so nothing outlives the check.
0696|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0697|         CHECK_STATUS=124
0698|     else
0699|         kill -TERM "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0700|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0701|     fi
0702|     CHECK_WATCHER=
0703|     CHECK_OUTPUT=$(cat "$out") || CHECK_OUTPUT=
0704|     cleanup_check
0705|     return 0
0706| }

0001| #!/bin/sh
0002| # Forgel Code installer.
0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:
0005| #
0006| #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.1.0/install.sh | sh
0007| #
0008| # The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
0009| # ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, under a hard time limit, and checks that
0017| # ``forgel-code`` resolves to the launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces the
0018| # installation; running with ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
0019| #
0020| # Environment variables:
0021| #   FORGEL_CODE_HOME            install prefix (default: $HOME/.local/share/forgel-code)
0022| #   FORGEL_CODE_BIN             launcher directory (default: $HOME/.local/bin)
0023| #   FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE          local checkout to install from, without network
0024| #   FORGEL_CODE_TAG             repository tag when no checkout is given (default: v0.1.0)
0025| #   FORGEL_CODE_REPOSITORY      repository URL used with FORGEL_CODE_TAG
0026| #   FORGEL_CODE_PYTHON          Python 3 interpreter (default: python3 on PATH)
0027| #   FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE         shell profile to edit (default: chosen from the login shell)
0028| #   FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH  set to leave the shell profile untouched
0029| #   FORGEL_CODE_NO_PROFILE_EDIT the same opt-out under its older name
0030| #   FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT         seconds the fresh-shell check may take (default: 10)
0031| #   FORGEL_CODE_VERIFY_GRACE    seconds between the graceful stop and the
0032| #                               forceful one when the bound elapses (default: 2)
0033| #   FORGEL_CODE_POLL_MS         how often, in milliseconds, the watchdog looks
0034| #                               at the checked process (default: 1000)
0035| #
0036| # The script is POSIX ``sh`` and safe to pipe into: it never reads stdin.
0037| 
0038| set -eu

0582| # Run a command under a hard time bound. ``timeout`` from GNU coreutils is not
0583| # required and is not used: the command runs in the background, a watchdog
0584| # sends a graceful stop when the bound elapses and forcefully stops whatever
0585| # remains of the process tree after the grace period, and the caller returns
0586| # as soon as the command itself is done. Nothing the function starts survives
0587| # it. CHECK_STATUS is 124 when the bound elapsed.

0589| # The checked command is deliberately *not* given its own process group here.
0590| # ``set -m`` makes the shell put the background job in a background process
0591| # group, and an interactive login shell in that position stops on its first
0592| # terminal access instead of answering, which is exactly the hang this check
0593| # must not have. The process tree walk in ``signal_run`` reaches everything the
0594| # shell forked without it.

0596|     limit=$1
0597|     shift
0598|     CHECK_STATUS=0
0599|     CHECK_OUTPUT=
0600|     if ! create_check_dir; then

0602|     fi
0603|     out=$CHECK_DIR/output
0604|     timed_out=$CHECK_DIR/timed-out
0605|     saved_umask=$(umask)
0606|     umask 077
0607|     if ! : > "$out"; then
0608|         umask "$saved_umask"
0609|         cleanup_check
0610|         return 1
0611|     fi
0612|     "$@" > "$out" 2>/dev/null < /dev/null &
0613|     CHECK_CHILD=$!
0614|     umask "$saved_umask"
0615|     child=$CHECK_CHILD

0617|         exec > /dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null
0618|         sleeper=
0619|         trap 'kill "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true; exit 0' TERM
0620|         elapsed=0

0622|             sleep 1 &
0623|             sleeper=$!
0624|             wait "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true
0625|             sleeper=
0626|             elapsed=$((elapsed + 1))
0627|             if ! kill -0 "$child" 2>/dev/null; then
0628|                 exit 0
0629|             fi
0630|         done
0631|         : > "$timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
0632|         signal_run TERM "$child"
0633|         sleep "$VERIFY_GRACE" 2>/dev/null || true
0634|         signal_run KILL "$child"

0636|     CHECK_WATCHER=$!
0637|     wait "$child" || CHECK_STATUS=$?
0638|     CHECK_CHILD=
0639|     if [ -e "$timed_out" ]; then
0640|         # The watchdog still owns the graceful then the forceful stop; let it
0641|         # finish so nothing outlives the check.
0642|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0643|         CHECK_STATUS=124
0644|     else
0645|         kill -TERM "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0646|         wait "$CHECK_WATCHER" 2>/dev/null || true
0647|     fi
0648|     CHECK_WATCHER=
0649|     CHECK_OUTPUT=$(cat "$out") || CHECK_OUTPUT=
0650|     cleanup_check
0651|     return 0
0652| }

1067| def _hanging_shell(directory: Path) -> Path:
1068|     """A handled shell name whose login session never finishes."""
1069|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1070|     stub = directory / "bash"

1076| def _stubborn_shell(directory: Path, pid_file: Path) -> Path:
1077|     """A handled shell name that never answers and ignores the graceful stop.
1078| 
1079|     It records its own pid first, so the test can prove the check left no
1080|     process behind once it returned.
1081|     """
1082|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1083|     stub = directory / "bash"
1084|     stub.write_text(
1085|         "#!/bin/sh\n"
1086|         'printf "%%s\\n" "$$" > %s\n' % _shell_quote(pid_file)
1087|         + "trap '' TERM\n"
1088|         + "while :; do sleep 1; done\n",
1089|         encoding="utf-8",
1090|     )
1091|     stub.chmod(0o755)
1092|     return stub
1093| 
1094| 
1095| def _recording_login_shell(directory: Path, probe: Path, real_shell: str) -> Path:
1096|     """A handled shell name that records the check's directory, then runs ``real_shell``.
1097| 
1098|     ``ls -ld`` output of every ``forgel-code-check.*`` entry goes into ``probe``,
1099|     so the test can inspect the permissions of a directory that no longer exists
1100|     by the time the installer returns. The entries sit in the temporary tree of
1101|     the test, next to the checked shell's own ``$HOME``.
1102|     """
1103|     directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1104|     stub = directory / "bash"
1105|     stub.write_text(
1106|         "#!/bin/sh\nprobe=%s\n" % _shell_quote(probe)
1107|         + 'ls -ld "$(dirname "$HOME")/tmp"/%s.* > "$probe/entries" 2>/dev/null || true\n'
1108|         % CHECK_PREFIX
1109|         + 'exec %s "$@"\n' % _shell_quote(real_shell),
1110|         encoding="utf-8",
1111|     )
1112|     stub.chmod(0o755)
1113|     return stub
